title: A Dead Star Flashed for 0.1 Seconds and Outshone 100,000 Years of Sun

scenes.text: A dead star released a hundred thousand years of sunlight in a blink.
On December twenty-seventh, 2004, a magnetar fifty thousand light-years away flared.
The flash lasted just over a tenth of a second.
In that instant it released more energy than our Sun gives off in a hundred thousand years.
The light even bounced off the Moon and lit up Earth's upper atmosphere.
A tenth of a second. A hundred thousand years.

description:
A magnetar 50,000 light-years away flared in 2004 and released more energy in a tenth of a second than our Sun gives off in 100,000 years.
The flash lit up Earth's upper atmosphere.
Could you picture 100,000 years of sunlight in a blink?
first_comment: Bonus: scientists say a flare like this within ten light-years would have seriously damaged our atmosphere. Glad it was 50,000 away?
